title: Digital Marketing Agency in Florida
metaTitle: Digital Marketing Agency in Florida | TDM
metaDescription: Digital marketing for Florida businesses: SEO, paid ads, social media, websites and video, planned around seasons, tourism and new residents.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works with Florida businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Florida's customers change with the month: residents all year, winter residents from the north, holidaymakers, cruise passengers and buyers from Latin America. We plan marketing around who is in the state, and in your part of it, at the time you need them.

sections.heading: A state that fills and empties with the seasons
paragraphs: In South and Southwest Florida the busy months are the cool ones. Part-time residents, often called snowbirds, arrive for the winter and leave in spring, and restaurants, clinics, golf clubs and contractors in places such as Naples, Sarasota and Palm Beach feel it in their bookings. The Panhandle works the other way round: Destin, Panama City Beach and Pensacola are summer destinations for families who drive in from neighbouring states.

Orlando has its own rhythm, tied to school holidays and the convention calendar. Hurricane season, from June to the end of November, adds a second layer. A storm can stop trade for days and then create urgent demand for roofers, tree services, restoration firms and insurance advice. A marketing plan for Florida needs a seasonal budget and a storm plan.

sections.heading: Florida's regions are separate markets
paragraphs: Distances are long, and a business in Jacksonville has little in common with one in Fort Lauderdale. We treat each metro on its own terms.
bullets: South Florida (Miami, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach): international in outlook, strong in real estate, finance, trade, cruises and hospitality.
Central Florida (Orlando, Kissimmee, Lakeland): theme parks, conventions, short-term rentals and fast-growing residential suburbs.
Tampa Bay (Tampa, St. Petersburg, Clearwater): a mix of healthcare, finance, beaches and a fast-growing residential market.
Northeast Florida (Jacksonville, St. Augustine): port and logistics, military families, and a more traditional Southern customer base.
Southwest Florida and the Panhandle: retirees and second-home owners on one coast, summer beach tourism on the other.

sections.heading: Who is searching: newcomers and retirees
paragraphs: Florida keeps drawing new residents from other states, many of them from the Northeast and Midwest. They arrive without a doctor, an insurance agent or a contractor, and they often start researching before the move, so searches for Florida services come from outside the state too. Newcomers also face questions that are particular to Florida, such as homeowners insurance, flood zones and storm preparation, and a business that answers those plainly on its site earns the first call.

Florida also has a large retired population. Older customers search and compare online like anyone else, but they tend to prefer a phone call to a form, read reviews carefully and respond to plain wording and legible pages. Sites for healthcare, legal, financial and home services should make the phone number obvious and the next step simple.

sections.heading: Where we usually begin
paragraphs: We look at your current customers, your service area and your calendar, then choose one main channel. For services booked in a hurry, that is local search and Google Ads. For restaurants, attractions, rentals and property, it is social media and short video, supported by an accurate Google Business Profile. Websites, tracking and creative are handled by the same team, so results are reported as money spent against money returned.

cards.heading: Florida industries and what they need

items.title: Tourism and attractions
items.text: Hotels, tours and attractions need to be found during trip planning, with ads timed to school holidays and winter travel.

items.title: Vacation rentals
items.text: Owners and managers in Orlando and on both coasts rely on photography, direct-booking sites and campaigns that reduce dependence on listing platforms.

items.title: Home services
items.text: Roofing, air conditioning, pool and restoration firms win on map rankings, reviews and ads that can be scaled up after a storm.

items.title: Healthcare and senior living
items.text: Practices and communities need clear pages, careful ad wording and an easy way to call.

items.title: Real estate and relocation
items.text: Agents, builders and movers market to people who are still living in another state or country.

presence: A member of our team is based in Miami. The wider team works remotely with businesses across Florida, from the Panhandle to the Keys, and delivers the strategy, design, development and video.

faqs.q: Does TDM have anyone in Florida?
faqs.a: Yes. A member of our team is based in Miami. Work for clients elsewhere in Florida is delivered remotely by the wider team, with regular calls and shared reporting.

faqs.q: How should a Florida business budget for the off-season?
faqs.a: Reduce spend on demand that is not there and use the quiet months for work that pays later: search content, reviews, site improvements and creative. The split depends on your trade and region and is set in the plan.

faqs.q: How should a Florida business prepare its marketing for hurricane season?
faqs.a: Write the pages, ad copy and customer messages before the season starts in June. Keep hours and closure notices current on your Google Business Profile, pause ads when you cannot take work, and restart them with accurate wording when you reopen.

faqs.q: How much do digital marketing services cost in Florida?
faqs.a: It depends on the scope of work, the channels and the competition in your area. We provide a quote after a free consultation.

faqs.q: Can you run campaigns in several Florida cities?
faqs.a: Yes. We set up separate keywords, landing pages, budgets and business profiles for each location, so Tampa is not competing with Orlando for the same spend.
